note: The City of Memphis government guide states that the mayor serves a four-year term and gives the next mayoral election as 2027. The regular mayoral cycle is therefore 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2027. The 2009 special election winner served the remainder of the term that ran to the 2011 election, so no mayoral election fell in 2010. The Election Commission archive has no 2010 page, so this rests on the term cycle.

The cycle in the City of Memphis government guide places a mayoral election in 2011, and secondary sources date it October 6, 2011. The Shelby County Election Commission past-elections archive starts in 2012 and has no 2011 page (the 2010 and 2011 year pages return HTTP 404). No official 2011 results document was found. The Internet Archive was offline (Temporarily Offline page) when tried. Secondary sources are not used for results. Second pass: the past-elections page https://www.electionsshelbytn.gov/past-elections/ returned HTTP 200 and has no 2011 link. https://www.electionsshelbytn.gov/past-elections/2011-past-elections/ and the 2010 equivalent returned HTTP 404. The Wayback CDX API returned no response with curl, and WebFetch refused web.archive.org. The web search quota was exhausted, so council minutes and state sources were not searched. The year stays unresolved.

The City of Memphis government guide states that the mayor serves a four-year term and gives the next mayoral election as 2027. The regular mayoral cycle is therefore 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2027. The Shelby County Election Commission past-elections page for this year lists no City of Memphis municipal mayoral election. The official statement of votes cast for the November general election was searched. It contains mayoral contests only for other Shelby County towns, none for Memphis.
